liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews, 1 other source): The closing exchange between Jerry and Keith is described as manic; Reviewer considers the Dark Star to be of high quality [1][5][7][13]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Pigpen's version is described as super-funky; Reviewer's favorite: a jazzy groove with stupendous lead from Jerry and a subdued rap from Pigpen [14][16]
- **Sing Me Back Home** (2 reviews): Singled out as the show's gem, comparable to the Veneta version, though Ron's organ sits very low in the mix; Reviewer calls it splendid: Jerry sings it well and his guitar tone is sweet; the song appears mostly in 1971-72 [5][6]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Keith is playing with particular feeling here, as on Chinatown Shuffle [8]
- **It Hurts Me Too** (1 review): Pigpen's work is called nice here, as on Mr. Charlie and Chinatown Shuffle [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.smith.94581.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 195 min [1]
- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.miller.79057.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 182 min; rated 4.91/5 by 11 [2]
- **gd72-05-18.sbd.unicorn.2266.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 177 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: Sounds muffled and not especially good, though still listenable; Reviewer says the soundboard seems updated and may be the best-sounding Europe '72 soundboard on the site, near perfect; The mix is even and the sound is described as great [6][7][8][11][12][13][14]
- **gd1972-05-18.sdb.lai.146.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 25 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer lived in Munich at age 19, having graduated from Munich American High, an army school, the previous year [9]
- Reviewer finds Donna's off-key singing annoying [12]
- Otherwise considered a fairly typical Europe '72 show [6]
- Reviewer rates late 1971 and early 1972 as Keith's best concerts, and finds this show unusually tight for the Dead [8]
- Reviewer says this show clarifies the Europe '72 hype, seeing the tour as a step toward exploration in Playin' and Truckin' [11]
- Show feels like one long first set with little jamming, apart from the atonal Dark Star and some Playin' licks [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.smith.94581.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rex Jackson; transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: Soundboard > Master Reel (Rex Jackson) [1]. Also: Matt Smith supplied the original discs; noise from reel generation was attenuated; edited using the GEMS Edit Station [1]
- **gd1972-05-18.sbd.miller.79057.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) D [2]. Also: Reviewer credits Miller for this soundboard mix of the show [16]
- **gd72-05-18.sbd.unicorn.2266.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSR> ?> dat> cdr [3]. Also: Lineage: MSR to unknown to DAT to CDR; a repaired version of an earlier shn set, passed from Mike (Unicorn) to abgd [3]
- **gd1972-05-18.sdb.lai.146.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: master reel>>sdb>>?>>dat>>cdr [4]
